messages:
Maria (AM): kicking off the FinTrust POC thread — they need Private deployment in their AWS account, must pass security questionnaire, and require a deterministic egress IP for allowlisting. timeline: 2-week POC.
Alex (SE): noted. primary ask: preserve client source IP to downstream services and support mutual TLS to our control plane. they also want guidance on PrivateLink vs VPC Peering.
Raj (NetOps): short answer: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) avoids route table exposure and keeps traffic inside AWS with NLBs. Peering could work but has limitations with cross-account overlapping CIDRs and doesn't provide a stable endpoint DNS for allowlists.
Maria (AM): they called out two blockers in the security questionnaire: 1) rotating egress IPs, 2) firewall rules for egress to our management/control plane.
Tim (Solutions Eng): can confirm egress IP rotation is a thing for shared hosted infra, but for Private customers we can recommend static egress via NAT Gateway or an NLB with Elastic IPs in their account. doc snippet:
```
# recommended pattern
- Deploy NAT Gateway(s) in the spoke subnets for egress
- Use EIP allocation per AZ for stable source IPs
- Route model inference outbound via these NATs
```
Raj (NetOps): + add: if they want source-ip preservation (client IP visible to your app) run the Redwood serving plane in their VPC (Private deployment) behind NLBs with proxy protocol v2 and set our connectors to passthrough. Otherwise NAT will SNAT.
Sophia (InfoSec): on the questionnaire point: they want an attestation that only required ports are open and that TLS 1.2+ is enforced. We should give specific firewall rules and a short cert/mTLS checklist.
Alex (SE): firewall rules we ask customers to allow outbound to:
- Control plane (management): 3x Egress FQDNs -> *.redwood-inference.com (443)
- Model pulls/updates: s3.amazonaws.com for AMI/model blobs (443) or our model registry endpoints
- Health & metrics sinks: optional, to their own endpoints
Example CIDR/IP guidance (customer-managed): prefer FQDN allowlists but if they need IPs: allocate EIPs from NAT per AZ and provide those.
Maria (AM): FinTrust specifically requires a one-page network diagram to attach to the questionnaire. Can someone mock one that shows: customer VPC -> subnet w/serving NLB -> private endpoints to S3 & KMS -> NAT + EIPs for egress?
Tim (Solutions Eng): I can sketch. Also point: PrivateLink option: they can create interface endpoints for our Private service in their account. That gives stable DNS hostnames: something like vpce-012345-abc.vpce-svc-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com. We should add an example curl test to validate connectivity.
Raj (NetOps): example test:
```
curl -v https://vpce-012345-abc.vpce-svc-xxxx.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: model.redwood-inference.com'
```
Alex (SE): add note: when using VPC endpoints with TLS inspection (corp proxies), SNI must be preserved — otherwise cert name mismatch. If they perform TLS inspect we need a bypass for our endpoint hostnames or mTLS to avoid MITM.
Sophia (InfoSec): security Q: Do we require customer to open inbound ports? No inbound from internet to service. Only inbound from their internal network to the NLB/serving subnets. Outbound: only 443 to the endpoints above. Provide this wording for questionnaire.
Maria (AM): pricing Q from FinTrust: will dedicated EIPs/NAT increase the POC cost? how do we pitch it?
Tim (Solutions Eng): yes, NAT Gateway + EIPs have AWS costs. Offer two POC patterns:
- Minimal: use an existing NAT/egress IP (cheapest), accept SNAT (lose client IP).
- Fully-isolated: provision NAT Gateway(s) + allocated EIPs (higher infra cost) and run Redwood Private in their VPC to preserve source IP. Provide monthly estimate: ~ $x/day per NAT gateway + EIP. (I'll attach a line-item offline).
Maria (AM): FinTrust also has a legal request: proof-of-encryption-in-transit + key custody for KMS. we should confirm KMS integration options (customer-managed CMKs vs Redwood-managed).
Alex (SE): we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. Note in questionnaire: "Customer KMS CMK ARN used for model key encryption; logs show KMS key usage".
Sophia (InfoSec): also include SOC2 / ISO attestation references and a short paragraph: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, VPC isolation, and audit logs; for hosted please reference SOC2 report". I'll paste cert links in the doc.
Raj (NetOps): one more technical gotcha: if they use VPC Peering across accounts and have overlapping CIDRs with other spokes, traffic to our infra may route incorrectly. recommend using PrivateLink or Transit Gateway to avoid overlapping CIDR issues.
Maria (AM): action items: 1) Tim to deliver one-page network diagram + example curl test (ETA today), 2) Raj to draft recommended firewall rules and NAT/EIP pattern (ETA EOD), 3) Sophia to draft the questionnaire language and attestation snippet (ETA tomorrow), 4) Alex to prepare a short note on KMS options for legal.
Tim (Solutions Eng): working on diagram now, will post PNG link and ASCII fallback.
deploy-bot: deploy status: POC sandbox infra ready in us-west-2 (build-982). :rocket:
Raj (NetOps): quick follow-up: if they want to use an SNI proxy we need them to confirm whether host-header passthrough is allowed. otherwise, we recommend mTLS to avoid SNI rewrite issues.
Maria (AM): thanks team — I'll present these options to FinTrust in tomorrow's call. please add any one-line clarifications here. :thumbsup:
Alex (SE): one-line to add for questionnaire: "All control plane traffic uses TLS 1.2+ and public FQDNs; customers can enforce egress via dedicated EIPs for allowlisting."
Sophia (InfoSec): and: "Customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; key usage is auditable via CloudTrail."
Maria (AM): perfect. closing the loop — will update the doc and share with FinTrust.
